core_obligations: Show that if F is a coherent O_X-module flat over Y with fibre supports of dimension at most r, G a coherent O_Y-module with support of delta-dimension at most e, alpha = [F/X/Y]_r and beta = [G]_e, then alpha cap beta = [F tensor f^*G]_{r+e} (proof lines 2373-2429). First, compute the support: Supp(F tensor f^*G) = Supp(F) intersect f^{-1}Supp(G) = union over y in Supp(G) of Supp(F_y), a closed subset of delta-dimension at most r+e, so the cycle class [F tensor f^*G]_{r+e} makes sense (proof lines 2374-2383). Second, using the notation beta = sum n_i [Z_i], y_i in Z_i, alpha_{y_i} = sum m_{ij} [V_{ij}] and the closures V-bar_{ij} introduced in the construction of alpha cap beta, observe that the Z_i are exactly the irreducible components of Supp(G) of delta-dimension e, the V_{ij} the irreducible components of Supp(F_{y_i}) of dimension r, and by the first paragraph the V-bar_{ij} are the irreducible components of Supp(F tensor f^*G) of delta-dimension r+e, so it suffices to prove the length identity length_{O_{X,xi}}((F tensor f^*G)_xi) = length_{O_{X_y,xi}}((F_y)_xi) times length_{O_{Y,y}}(G_y) at the generic points xi (proof lines 2385-2408). Third, by the first paragraph the left hand side is the length of the B = O_{X,xi}-module G_y tensor_{O_{Y,y}} F_xi = M tensor_A N, where M = G_y is a finite length A = O_{Y,y}-module and N = F_xi is a finite B-module with N/m_A N of finite length, flat over A since F is flat over Y; the right hand side equals length_B(N/m_A N) times length_A(M); both sides are additive in M using the flatness of N over A, so it suffices to verify the formula for M = the residue field of A, where it is immediate (proof lines 2409-2428).
proof_roadmap: Support computation: the tensor product has support the union of the fibre supports, closed of delta-dimension at most r+e, so the target cycle class is defined (proof lines 2374-2383).
Component identification via the construction notation reduces the lemma to a length identity at the generic points (proof lines 2385-2408).
Algebra: both sides of the length identity are additive in the finite length module M thanks to flatness of N over A, reducing to the residue field case (proof lines 2409-2428).
